title: Union-find: counting connected groups
summary: Give every group a leader; join groups by pointing one leader at the other, smaller under larger.
note: Undirected edges between nodes 0 to n - 1.

narration.text: Every node starts as its own group and its own leader: parent = {parent}.
Every group starts with one node.
Define find: follow parent links up to the group's leader.
{x} isn't a leader: its parent is {parent[x]}.
{x} is its own parent, so it's the leader.
Path halving: point {x} at its grandparent, {parent[x]}, to shorten later searches.
Move up to {x}.
The leader is {x}.
{components} separate groups to start with.
Edge {u} – {v}: their groups should become one.
Every edge has been processed.
{u}'s leader is {ru}, and {v}'s leader is {rv}.
Same leader: {u} and {v} are already in the same group.
Different leaders: merge the two groups.
Nothing to merge.
{ru}'s group has {size[ru]} nodes, fewer than {rv}'s {size[rv]}: swap, so the bigger group's leader stays leader.
{ru}'s group has {size[ru]} nodes, at least as many as {rv}'s {size[rv]}, so {ru} stays leader.
Now {ru} leads the bigger group.
Point {rv} at {ru}: the two groups are now one.
The merged group has {size[ru]} nodes.
One group fewer: {components} left.
There are {components} connected groups.
